claims.text: A simplified neural text matching architecture can maintain effective inter-sequence alignment by combining original point-wise features, previous aligned features, and contextual features.
The proposed text matching approach achieves an inference speed at least 6 times faster than similarly performing models.

evidence.description: The authors propose to keep three key features available for inter-sequence alignment: original point-wise features, previous aligned features, and contextual features while simplifying all the remaining components.
The inference speed is at least 6 times faster compared with similarly performed ones.

methodologies.name: Simplified Rich Alignment Neural Text Matching Model
methodologies.description: A fast neural text matching model that retains point-wise, previously aligned, and contextual features for sequence alignment while simplifying other architectural components.
